title: Adaptive reservoir sampling + curator workflow for config-sensitive golden sets
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Background: We rely on static golden sets to detect quality regressions during model and config rollouts. As models/configs diversify, static lists either grow unmanageably large or become stale for specific workload slices. This ticket designs an adaptive golden-reservoir plus curator workflow that maintains a bounded, representative set of golden examples per config-variant while preserving auditability and access controls.

Goals: Maintain a small (config-scoped) golden reservoir that: 1) surfaces likely regression-sensitive samples for new model/config variants using lightweight signal heuristics; 2) allows curators to accept/reject/annotate candidates via a simple UI; 3) produces immutable, signed snapshots used by eval pipelines and rollout gates; 4) ties selection provenance to config changes so we can trace why a sample is in a given reservoir.

Scope:
- Design reservoir selection algorithm (hybrid: reservoir sampling seeded by delta-detection + priority reweighting for low-frequency failure modes).
- Add a curator micro-UI in Console for bulk review, tagging, and severity scoring (accept/reject/hold).
- Produce signed snapshot artifacts stored in blob + ledger entries for immutability and CI reproducibility.
- Add hooks in eval-orchestrator to load config-scoped reservoirs and compute regression deltas during pre-rollout and continuous monitoring.
- Enforce ACLs and curator audit trail: who curated, when, and decision rationale.

Out-of-scope (for this ticket): automated model-led labelling, full active-learning retraining loops, or multi-customer merged reservoirs.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Reservoir size target: 1k per config-variant upper bound. Small size keeps eval cost predictable and allows manual curation.
- Algorithm choices: full active sampling (high recall) vs. heuristic delta-seeding (low compute). We choose delta-seeding for initial rollout to limit compute and complexity, with a flag to enable heavier sampling in nightly jobs.
- Signed snapshots vs. database row-level immutability: snapshots (tar + signature) simplify reproducibility for CI and allow easy storage in existing blob store. Ledger row entries provide quick lookup for UI.
- Curator UX: allow bulk accept with templated rationale to speed reviews, but require at-least-one-comment for rejects to avoid silent deletions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Reservoir generator runs in CI for a given config-change and produces a candidate list within budget (<= 200 CPU-seconds).
- Curator UI can display candidate list, persist decisions, and export a signed snapshot.
- Eval-orchestrator can consume signed snapshots and produce regression metrics used by rollout gate jobs.
- End-to-end demo: config-change -> reservoir candidate generation -> curator approval -> snapshot consumed by canary eval -> alert on regression (simulated).
